title: The Vertebrate Readers: DCC and UNC5

scenes.tts: The worm found two readers for one cue. Do vertebrate growth cones use the same ones?
scenes.visual: Title card: The Vertebrate Readers. A worm growth cone and a rat growth cone side by side. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: The worm found two readers for one cue. Do vertebrate growth cones use the same ones?

scenes.tts: Back on the spinal cord map, follow the commissural axons to the floor plate.
scenes.visual: The transverse spinal cord map: dorsal commissural neurons at top, floor plate at the ventral midline, ventricular zone around the central canal, pial surface at the outer edge, commissural path drawn from dorsal cord down near the pia, then in across the floor plate. The commissural growth cone is highlighted on its way in.
scenes.narration: Back on the spinal cord map, follow the commissural axons to the floor plate.

scenes.tts: The worm's toward reader, U N C forty, turned out to resemble a human protein. Its name is D C C, Deleted in Colorectal Cancer.
scenes.caption: The worm's toward reader, UNC-40, turned out to resemble a human protein. Its name is DCC, Deleted in Colorectal Cancer.
scenes.visual: UNC-40 and DCC drawn as matching receptors. Label: DCC, Deleted in Colorectal Cancer.
scenes.narration: The worm's toward reader, UNC-40, turned out to resemble a human protein. Its name is DCC, Deleted in Colorectal Cancer.

scenes.tts: It was first studied as a cancer gene.
scenes.visual: A small inset: chromosome 18 with a stretch marked, and a colon tissue icon.
scenes.narration: It was first studied as a cancer gene.

scenes.tts: In nineteen ninety-six, Tessier-Lavigne's laboratory tested D C C in rat embryos, spinal explants and cultured cells. They showed three things.
scenes.caption: In 1996, Tessier-Lavigne's laboratory tested DCC in rat embryos, spinal explants and cultured cells. They showed three things.
scenes.visual: Label: 1996. A rat embryo section, a dish of spinal explants and a dish of cultured cells. Three empty numbered boxes.
scenes.narration: In 1996, Tessier-Lavigne's laboratory tested DCC in rat embryos, spinal explants and cultured cells. They showed three things.

scenes.tts: First, D C C is on commissural axons.
scenes.caption: First, DCC is on commissural axons.
scenes.visual: Box 1: commissural axons on the map stained for DCC.
scenes.narration: First, DCC is on commissural axons.

scenes.tts: Second, netrin one binds cultured cells that display D C C.
scenes.caption: Second, netrin-1 binds cultured cells that display DCC.
scenes.visual: Box 2: cultured cells with DCC on their surface; netrin-1 sticks to them.
scenes.narration: Second, netrin-1 binds cultured cells that display DCC.

scenes.tts: Third, they added an antibody that blocks D C C to spinal explants with netrin. What should happen to the outgrowth?
scenes.caption: Third, they added an antibody that blocks DCC to spinal explants with netrin. What should happen to the outgrowth?
scenes.visual: Box 3: an explant with netrin and an antibody drawn over the DCC receptors. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Third, they added an antibody that blocks DCC to spinal explants with netrin. What should happen to the outgrowth?

scenes.tts: The antibody selectively blocked netrin evoked outgrowth from the spinal explants.
scenes.caption: The antibody selectively blocked netrin-evoked outgrowth from the spinal explants.
scenes.visual: Bar chart: no netrin, low; netrin, high; netrin with anti-DCC, low. Label: selective block.
scenes.narration: The antibody selectively blocked netrin-evoked outgrowth from the spinal explants.

scenes.tts: In the same journal issue, worm work showed that U N C forty is needed in the moving cells themselves.
scenes.caption: In the same journal issue, worm work showed that UNC-40 is needed in the moving cells themselves.
scenes.visual: A worm cell migrating, with UNC-40 marked on the cell itself.
scenes.narration: In the same journal issue, worm work showed that UNC-40 is needed in the moving cells themselves.

scenes.tts: The mouse confirmed both partners. Mice with little or no netrin one had misrouted spinal commissural axons.
scenes.caption: The mouse confirmed both partners. Mice with little or no netrin-1 had misrouted spinal commissural axons.
scenes.visual: Two spinal cord maps side by side. Left, normal. Right, netrin-1 mutant: commissural axons wander off the path.
scenes.narration: The mouse confirmed both partners. Mice with little or no netrin-1 had misrouted spinal commissural axons.

scenes.tts: They also lacked several forebrain commissures. Mice lacking D C C had similar defects.
scenes.caption: They also lacked several forebrain commissures. Mice lacking DCC had similar defects.
scenes.visual: A third map, Dcc mutant, with similar wandering axons. A forebrain outline with missing crossing bundles.
scenes.narration: They also lacked several forebrain commissures. Mice lacking DCC had similar defects.

scenes.tts: Remove the cue or remove the reader, and commissural axons fail in much the same way.
scenes.visual: The two mutant maps overlay and match. Label: no cue, or no reader.
scenes.narration: Remove the cue or remove the reader, and commissural axons fail in much the same way.

scenes.tts: Now repulsion. In nineteen ninety-five, netrin one repelled trochlear motor axons in explant cultures.
scenes.caption: Now repulsion. In 1995, netrin-1 repelled trochlear motor axons in explant cultures.
scenes.visual: Label: 1995. A midbrain-hindbrain inset: trochlear axons in a gel turn away from a netrin source.
scenes.narration: Now repulsion. In 1995, netrin-1 repelled trochlear motor axons in explant cultures.

scenes.tts: So the second puzzle is real in vertebrates. Different growth cones, same cue, opposite turns. The worm already suggested why: different readers.
scenes.visual: The transverse spinal cord map: dorsal commissural neurons at top, floor plate at the ventral midline, ventricular zone around the central canal, pial surface at the outer edge, commissural path drawn from dorsal cord down near the pia, then in across the floor plate. Box 2 fills: different growth cones, same cue, opposite turns.
scenes.narration: So the second puzzle is real in vertebrates. Different growth cones, same cue, opposite turns. The worm already suggested why: different readers.

scenes.tts: In the netrin one mutant, though, trochlear axons were largely normal. Other repellents also guide them.
scenes.caption: In the netrin-1 mutant, though, trochlear axons were largely normal. Other repellents also guide them.
scenes.visual: In a midbrain-hindbrain inset of the mutant, trochlear axons follow a near-normal route. Label: other repellents too.
scenes.narration: In the netrin-1 mutant, though, trochlear axons were largely normal. Other repellents also guide them.

scenes.tts: The fly shows how the repulsive reader works. Its U N C five receptor is a repulsive netrin receptor.
scenes.caption: The fly shows how the repulsive reader works. Its Unc5 receptor is a repulsive netrin receptor.
scenes.visual: A fly embryo nerve cord; a growth cone with Unc5 turns away from netrin.
scenes.narration: The fly shows how the repulsive reader works. Its Unc5 receptor is a repulsive netrin receptor.

scenes.tts: U N C five alone is enough for short-range repulsion. Long-range repulsion also needs Frazzled, the fly's D C C family receptor.
scenes.caption: Unc5 alone is enough for short-range repulsion. Long-range repulsion also needs Frazzled, the fly's DCC-family receptor.
scenes.visual: Two panels: short range, Unc5 alone; long range, Unc5 with Frazzled.
scenes.narration: Unc5 alone is enough for short-range repulsion. Long-range repulsion also needs Frazzled, the fly's DCC-family receptor.

scenes.tts: So the receptor layer reads like this. D C C draws a growth cone in. U N C five receptors add repulsion.
scenes.caption: So the receptor layer reads like this. DCC draws a growth cone in. UNC5 receptors add repulsion.
scenes.visual: Rule card: DCC, toward; UNC5, away.
scenes.narration: So the receptor layer reads like this. DCC draws a growth cone in. UNC5 receptors add repulsion.

scenes.tts: Treat that as a starting point. D C C family receptors also take part in some repulsion. And netrin has other receptors and partners.
scenes.caption: Treat that as a starting point. DCC-family receptors also take part in some repulsion. And netrin has other receptors and partners.
scenes.visual: Under the rule card, a tag: starting point. Small extra receptors appear around netrin.
scenes.narration: Treat that as a starting point. DCC-family receptors also take part in some repulsion. And netrin has other receptors and partners.

scenes.tts: The takeaway: the cue is shared, and the receptors a growth cone carries set the first answer.
scenes.visual: The transverse spinal cord map: dorsal commissural neurons at top, floor plate at the ventral midline, ventricular zone around the central canal, pial surface at the outer edge, commissural path drawn from dorsal cord down near the pia, then in across the floor plate. Takeaway on screen: the receptors set the first answer.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: the cue is shared, and the receptors a growth cone carries set the first answer.
